title: create_fragment_sender maps all SCHC decode failures to InvalidPeerEvidence
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs create_fragment_sender

Canonical-packet validation does:

  decode_rule255(..., SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE).ok()
  or peer.decompress(..., MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SCHC_PACKET).ok()
  then if None { return Err(FragmentError::InvalidPeerEvidence) }

Two defects:

1. Every failure becomes InvalidPeerEvidence ('stale or foreign peer evidence'), including TooShort, InvalidPacket, UnknownRuleId, and BufferTooSmall. Python raises 'fragmented packet must be a canonical complete SCHC packet'. Callers that treat InvalidPeerEvidence as 're-admit DIO / drop peer' will mis-handle truncated or unknown-rule payloads.

2. Rule 255 is decoded into a [u8; SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED] (1500) stack buffer while the profile limit passed in is SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554). A valid uncompressed packet with IPv6 > 1500 and payload.len() <= receiver_limit therefore fails closed as InvalidPeerEvidence instead of being fragmented. FragmentSender::new already enforces receiver_limit and MAX_PACKET_SIZE.

Preserve the real SchcError/FragmentError (or map packet errors to EmptyPacket/PacketTooLarge/UnsupportedRule). Decode into a buffer of min(receiver_limit, SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE) or skip materializing IPv6 beyond validate_full_ipv6 / decompress into caller-sized storage.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed or truncated SCHC payloads return a packet/rule error, not InvalidPeerEvidence, and do not reserve a sender. A canonical Rule 255 packet with IPv6 larger than 1500 and within receiver_limit/SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE creates a sender. Stale/foreign peer evidence still returns InvalidPeerEvidence via FragmentSender::new.
